planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in humus-rich, acidic soil in a sheltered spot with morning shade; raised at RHS Garden Wisley in 1946 and named for the garden's then-superintendent.

directions: Francis Hanger carries single, pure white flowers about three inches across with a dense central cluster of golden stamens, opening against glossy dark green foliage from early to mid spring. Growth is slow and compact at first, gradually forming a dense, rounded bush that suits a container or a tight garden corner better than most williamsii hybrids. Plant in moist, well-drained acidic soil with some shelter from drying wind, and mulch the shallow root zone to conserve moisture through summer. Deadhead spent blooms and prune lightly right after flowering to maintain its naturally neat shape.

planting.note: Raised at Tregrehan in Cornwall from a cross of two williamsii-group parents; plant in neutral-to-acid, humus-rich soil in part shade.

directions: China Clay produces striking semi-double white flowers up to four inches across, each centered on a prominent boss of golden stamens, over a medium-sized rounded shrub. Named for the Cornish clay-pit country near its birthplace, it earned an RHS Award of Merit for the clarity and substance of its bloom. Grow in moist but free-draining acidic soil with shelter from harsh midday sun, which can bleach the white petals. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer after flowering and keep the root zone mulched through dry summer stretches.

planting.note: A late-season New Zealand-raised williamsii hybrid named for the wife of Trehane Nursery's founder; site away from early morning sun to protect buds from frost damage.

directions: Joan Trehane bears large, clear rose-pink flowers that range from rose-form to formal double, up to five inches across, over dark green foliage from March into April. Young plants grow upright and somewhat open, filling in to a dense, spreading habit as they mature into a sizeable specimen shrub. Shelter from cold, drying winds and early morning sun, since late frosts can mar both buds and open flowers. Propagate from semi-hardwood cuttings and keep the root zone consistently moist but never waterlogged.

planting.note: Bred by Les Jury in New Plymouth, New Zealand, from a cross with Camellia japonica 'Daikagura'; first flowered in 1971.

directions: Mona Jury produces large peony-form flowers in apricot-pink, their 16 to 22 heavily veined petals set off by yellow anthers and white filaments, over light green foliage on an open-habited shrub. Bloom stretches from early into the later part of the camellia season, giving a longer display window than many single-flush cultivars. Give it part shade and humus-rich, acidic soil, and stake young plants loosely since the open growth habit can be slow to self-support. Thin crowded interior growth after flowering to keep air moving through the canopy.

planting.note: A seedling selection from Camellia x williamsii 'Rendezvous' raised by New Plymouth breeder Les Jury; grow in acidic, well-drained soil in part shade.

directions: Les Jury carries large double to peony-form flowers in deep crimson-red, often four inches wide with 75 or more petals and numerous petaloids, blooming from early into late winter. Its strong, upright growth and dense dark green foliage make it one of the sturdier williamsii hybrids for hedging or as a tall screen. Plant in humus-rich acidic soil with reliable moisture, and shelter from strong wind while young to protect the heavy blooms. Prune only lightly right after flowering so next season's bud set is not disturbed.

planting.note: A reticulata x saluenensis hybrid registered in New Zealand in 1958, named for the breeder's daughter; grow in acidic, well-drained soil in part shade.

directions: Barbara Clark bears clear rose-madder pink, semi-double flowers with notched petals arranged hose-in-hose, roughly three to three and a half inches across, opening from late winter into early spring. The upright shrub carries glossy dark green foliage and can reach substantial size over time, making a good background or specimen planting. Its reticulata parentage gives extra-large, long-lasting blooms but slightly less cold hardiness than pure williamsii types, so site it with some wind shelter in colder zones. Keep soil consistently moist and acidic, and mulch to protect the shallow root system.

planting.note: One of the early Caerhays-line williamsii hybrids, grown for its soft pink color and unusually long bloom season; grow in acidic, humus-rich soil in part shade.

directions: Lady Gowrie opens soft, fuchsine-pink flowers over glossy dark green foliage, with a notably extended bloom season that can run from late autumn through winter and into early spring in mild climates. The shrub grows into a substantial, well-furnished specimen that holds its shape with only light annual pruning after flowering. Plant in moist, well-drained acidic soil and provide some shelter from harsh winter wind to protect buds through the long flowering window. An acid-forming fertilizer applied after the main flush supports strong repeat budding the following year.

planting.note: A 1970s williamsii-group introduction prized for flowers held unusually well on the bush; grow in acidic, well-drained soil in part shade.

directions: Muskoka produces large semi-double to peony-form flowers in rose pink, sometimes striped with deeper red, opening fairly flat and displayed well above the dark green foliage during March and April. It makes a large, bushy evergreen shrub that tolerates severe winter cold better than most reticulata-leaning hybrids, having earned recognition for garden merit. Grow in humus-rich, acidic soil with consistent moisture and part shade, avoiding exposed sites where winter wind can desiccate foliage. Prune minimally and only right after bloom to preserve next year's flower buds.

planting.note: A chance seedling of 'Tali Queen' that originated at Shade & Shadow Nursery in Mountain View, California, and was registered with the American Camellia Society in 1967; grow in acidic, well-drained soil in part shade.

directions: Mandalay Queen bears huge semi-double, rose-pink flowers nearly six inches across with roughly 38 broad petals, a few petaloids, and bright yellow anthers, typical of the outsized blooms reticulata camellias are prized for. The shrub grows tall and somewhat open, benefiting from light staking and structural pruning while young to build a sturdy framework for its heavy flowers. It is less cold-hardy than japonica or williamsii types, so site it in a sheltered, part-shaded spot protected from hard freezes and drying wind. Keep the soil acidic, humus-rich, and evenly moist, and feed after the bloom flush to support the following season's bud set.
